findings.location: Every page of the PDF; TOC paragraphs P14-P61 of the DOCX; code/build_report_final.py CSS '.doc table{...table-layout:fixed;width:453.6pt...}'
findings.finding: The PDF twin is printed at about 92%: body text measures 10.1 pt (TimesNewRomanPSMT 10.1 for 86,416 characters; captions and tables 8.2 pt; Heading 1 12.8 pt; line pitch 11.7 pt) instead of the required Times New Roman 11 pt. Cause reproduced: Chromium shrinks the whole document because of the fixed-layout tables in the HTML twin (reprinting the same HTML without tables, or with 'width:100%;max-width:100%' instead of 'table-layout:fixed;width:453.6pt', gives 11.0 pt). Consequences: the PDF breaks the 11 pt requirement; its 42 pages understate the true length (48 pages at 11 pt); the TOC page numbers written into the DOCX were read from this shrunk PDF (References 'page 29' in the TOC against page 33 at 11 pt) and word/settings.xml has no updateFields flag, so Word shows wrong page numbers until the field is updated.
findings.fix: In code/build_report_final.py replace the table CSS 'table-layout:fixed;width:453.6pt' by 'width:100%;max-width:100%' (tested: 11.0 pt, 48 pages) or export the PDF from the DOCX with WPS Office; then recompute the TOC page numbers from that PDF and add <w:updateFields w:val="true"/> to word/settings.xml so Word refreshes the TOC on opening.
